newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt higher in listless pre-Christmas trade.
newsitem.headline: German debt higher in listless pre-Christmas trade.

text.p: German Bunds were higher late in the day, drifting in narrow ranges ahead of a three-day market holiday starting on Tuesday.
Traders said there was little to no investor interest and that they expected Bunds to remain around current levels when trade reopens on Friday.

The DTB Bund futures contract was up 14 basis points late in the day at 100.57 after trading in a range between 100.42 and 100.64. A statistic office report that West German preliminary average 1996 consumer prices climbed only 1.4 percent had little impact on Bunds.
Traders said the figures were in line with expectations and that inflation played little role in the Bundesbank's thinking about interest rates at the moment anyway.
Treasuries, which were also steady, contributed to the Bund market's sluggishness. The spread between Bunds and T-notes was steady around 64 basis points late in the day.
